title: Asked by parda-2d: Adopt the small vectors, matrices and batched kernels prototyped in parda-2d, close the Mat4-inverse gap, and offer a lean build
body:
Adopt the small vectors, matrices and batched kernels prototyped in parda-2d, close the Mat4-inverse gap, and offer a lean build (graft:01a10a64-df87..886a, from parda-2d)

What was needed:
- parda-2d: (1) Move parda-2d's crates/autodyne-math (github.com/vaibhav-gopal/parda2D at 7912896; written against autodyne fb75c4a) into autodyne as a module: Vec2/Vec3/Vec4, Mat3, Mat4 generic over Float (repr(C), column-major, bytemuck Pod for f32 and f64), products, transpose, determinant, inverses, rotations, translation, scale, project_point3, and compose_world (world[i] = world[parent[i]] * local[i] in one pass). f32 on x86-64 takes SSE paths for single products (chosen by TypeId, compiled away per instance); the batched kernel keeps plain arithmetic, which vectorizes better in its loop. Measured against glam (1,024 ops, quiet machine): compose_world 27.7/283 us vs 28.3/289 us for 10k/100k nodes (about 2% faster), Mat3 inverse 2.67 vs 2.80 us (about 4% faster), Mat4 * Mat4 4.27 vs 4.30 us and Mat4 * Vec4 600 vs 595 ns (parity), Mat4 inverse 9.6 vs 7.3 us (32% slower: scalar cofactors against glam's SSE). (2) A SIMD Mat4 inverse at least as fast as glam's. (3) NEON (aarch64) and wasm simd128 paths alongside SSE. (4) A lean build: these modules (with units and simd) usable without the rest; today autodyne with default-features = false still takes about 90 s to compile in release, which parda's users and wasm builds would pay for a sliver of the crate: a feature set or a small split crate. (5) Later, as parda needs them: lane-wise damped-spring and tween kernels over SoA arrays (M4), and portable f32x4/x8/x16 lanes with runtime dispatch for the software rasterizer (DESIGN.md section 16). (6) Published to crates.io under the library combination.

Answer (done): Built in autodyne's main branch (local commits, pushed when the user says), each measured in bench/geometry with results checked first. (1) and (2): autodyne::geometry, as answered on your details graft (Mat4 inverse 1.25x glam). (3) NEON and wasm simd128 single-value paths, tested on CI's arm and wasm jobs. (4) The lean build: autodyne = { default-features = false } now compiles only units, simd and geometry: a cold wasm32 release build in 5 s (1.5 MB rlib), against about 65 s with the DSP modules (features = ["dsp"] adds them back). (5) M4's kernels: geometry::Springs (columns of position, velocity and target with shared presets, SpringConfig::from_response or from_physical; the exact closed form for every damping regime and any dt; retargeting keeps position and velocity; settled() lists the lanes that came to rest each step; 5.3x a loop of per-lane transitions), geometry::Tweens with Ease (quad, cubic, expo in / out / in-out, CSS cubic-bezier by Newton with bisection; level with a plain loop: a convenience), and geometry::transform_points (homographies over x / y columns, 1.2x glam's per-point loop). The rasterizer: simd::lanes (F32x4 / F32x8 / F32x16) and simd::Level, and geometry::raster: RoundedRect::distance (and sixteen pixels at once), coverage = saturate(0.5 - d / w), fill_rounded_rect (premultiplied source-over into RGBA8 rows, the instruction set chosen at run time): 3.5x a plain loop with SSE2, 6.7x with AVX2, 9x with AVX-512, the same bytes at every level. Caveat for your wasm build: without std the row kernel's square root is libm's, per pixel (core has no f32::sqrt), so a no-std wasm build doesn't get vector square roots there yet; it's a todo here. (6) Publishing to crates.io is the user's call (a todo on them).
